text_fidelity_a: Selore&S-Global USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter 4K @60hz, Type C to HDMI Converter for MacBook Pro Air 2020/2019/2018,LenovoYoga 920/Thinkpad T480,Dell XPS 13/15,etc… I’ve had this for 8 months with no issues, then I got an under-the-desk treadmill and the screens go black and immediately come back on ALL THE TIME. I’ve tried using different plug ins for the treadmill and computer, not it (my husband is an electrician and assured me this was not it.). When testing this theory and intentionally removing power and plugging back in, the monitor had a setting box pup-up…. Because it lost powder, great. But when the screen flashes that box doesn’t come up which tells me it’s not loosing power-it’s loosing a connection to the computer. After messing with it and becoming frustrated, I thought I heard a little zap noise where it’s located so when I started feeling around I got a very minor static shock on my finger. So my Inspector Gadget hat told me that I was generating static electricity with my treadmill and for some reason it was collecting on this dual monitor plug and basically shorting itself out. (This only happens when walking on the treadmill.) So, in all my Mom-knowing madness, I wrapped it up in a dryer sheet and it actually works for the most part. It might flash a couple times in a day but my office smells amazing. I will be looking for something else for sure. It’s really annoying.
text_fidelity_b: Selore&S-Global USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter 4K @60hz, Type C to HDMI Converter for MacBook Pro Air 2020/2019/2018,LenovoYoga 920/Thinkpad T480,Dell XPS 13/15,etc…

PHILIPS Active Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth H6506 Flat Folding Lightweight Over Ear Wireless Headphones w/Multipoint Bluetooth Connection 30h Playtime with Deep Bass for Home/Office They did a quality job on these. Luxury without excess. Packaging is acceptable. The case feels great, the zipper is awesome. The headphones fit in very easily, and there is a mesh pouch inside for accessories.

The headphones have a giant L and R printed on the interior foam, which is convenient to figure out which way to put them on, but isn't visible once they are. The buttons are easy to access, labeled, and simple enough to remember.

I've tried a few modern wireless noise cancelling headphones, and I'd say some of the others win in one feature or another, but these are an excellent complete package.

text_fidelity_a:
Manfrotto 3-Way Pan/Tilt Head with RC2 Quick Release Plate (MH804-3WUS) I am writing one review for my entire purchase - it just makes sense that you know about the entire setup.

I bought the Manfrotto 808RC4 along with their 190XPROB Pro Tripod and the Manfrotto MB MSTRAP-1 Tripod Carrying Strap. All at Amazon. Here's why:

This head gives you unlimited control in all directions. The large knurled handles allow you to grip and adjust the tension on the pivot points to any degree you want. I use it to pan video, I use it to do off center composure and metering. I love how rock steady this thing is when I am shooting my 60and 120 second exposures with my 300MM lens. Rock steady. And the rotation is greased smooth, nary a glitch.

With a bubble level and two straight levels you always know where you are. And gradients to indicate -30 to +90 tilt for replication. Great for panning video or shooting stills for a panorama. There are two "softening springs" to slow the movement of the tilts as you reach either end. You can disengage them if you wish.

I have friends that went with the ball heads. And regret it. They are fast, but not accurate, especially with a long lens. With this head you can adjust the tension and just ease the camera around without having to adjust it again.

Now hear me on this. I see other reviewers not so happy with the way the shoe is a little tricky. Let me say that by practicing with the shoe mounted to your camera and paying close attention snap it onto the head three times and you know all you need to know. You may have to practice a few more times to get it in the dark but I tell you that you are going to love it. When you snap the camera onto the head it automatically engages and you have no worries. The double safety has stopped me from dropping my camera twice. Lesson learned at no cost.

As to the tripod - sturdy is the word that comes to mind. And NOT overly weighty. Together the head and tripod are 7 lbs. With the strap - which I did not buy at first - this rig is rock solid and you won't even know you are carrying it. I don't even notice the combo. I hike several hours at a time and have been know to stop in a panic on the way out and feel on my back to see if the whole thing is still there! I think a big part of the "weight" issue is how it is carried. In your hands it feels hefty. On your hips, 7 lbs feels weighty. Across your shoulder diagonally, head down? It ain't even there!

The tripod has a wonderfully steady center column assembly that comes up and tilts over to the horizontal - great for macro shots or simply needing to place the camera where you aren't. The legs are sturdy and the snap retainers have just the right tension - not too hard to snap open or closed, not so loose that you worry whether one might slide. I also like that the center column is not attached to the legs with the typical arms of lesser well made tripods. Makes for very easy folding and stowing. I love the leg angle presets - easy to use and not worried about them slipping. The rubber grips on two of the legs are a hand saver in chilly weather. Nice touch.

So, in case you haven't figured it out, I love this rig. If I were going trekking across country for days I might want a little less weight, but for day long trips, portraiture or car trips this is the ticket.

Bose SoundTrue around-ear wired headphones II - Apple devices, Navy Blue When I shop for headphones, I shop primarily for comfort. I’m not a sound snob -- I just need headphones that are super comfortable.

I’ve had a few pairs of over-ear/around-ear headphones. If I wear them too long, they give me a headache, either because they are too heavy after a while or squeeze too much or both. My last was a pair of Skullcandy’s, Hesh style, and I couldn’t wear them for more than 2-3 hours. These Bose SoundTrue’s feel a little lighter, and the ear cups are oval, not round, which makes them fit me better. They also don’t feel as tight on my head as the Skullcandy’s, but I don’t feel like they’re going to fall off.

Soundwise, I think they’re fine. But as I said, I’m not a sound snob, so as long as music sounds good and not like it’s played through a tin can, I’m happy.

Convenience wise, the ear cups swivel so the headphones fit in the included flat case. They don’t fold up a lot, but the case will be handy for when I want to take the headphones out with me. The cord is detachable, and has a remote for music/phone call control. I received the Apple version to review, so only the play/pause worked on my phone, but the other functions worked on my Macbook Air.

It's always the same, I need one for immediate situational biz use. I'm familiar with the step function tech advancements that arrive at this level of sophistication at the same price point as years ago.

From box to use was like 10 minutes. At an expendable price, I don't know how you could get more value. The advertised item is spot on for its bells and whistles. 2K vs. 4K is academic for my purpose. The camcorder is certainly delivering a higher than HD quality video with sound.

Anyone buying a camcorder at this price should know what to expect. My expectations were fairly low from experience. It's not going to be a family legacy Super-8. I'm shocked (shocked! I tell you) at just how much tech is packed in this palm video camera. The price doesn't include a typical 256G micro SD U1-3.

ORDRO seems to specialize in entry-level movie maker kits (I'm not). This electronic engine is scaled up into their $600 rigs.

Quite impressed.

I have an XL size glove hand for comparison in the image.

Weekend Update: Shot about 15 minutes @ 2k record. The superb image on the 1080p laptop display is the best true color I've seen ... the iPhone 11 color capture isn't this good. The sensitive sound recording picks up everything. Computer hook-up is intuitive. The laptop picks up the SD card (still in the camera) through the USB port like a thumb drive. MS video viewer downloads. plays and files as usual. Haven't needed any software to get this far ... which is as far as I need it.

Was my review helpful? If so, click "Helpful" so I can know. I'm trying hard to increase the value of my reviews to assist in your selection.

I bought them to use as curtains for my master bedroom and, for that, they are perfect!

They are very lightweight, almost obliquely translucent at times, and they aren't stitched super well (there are little threads you'll need to clip), but otherwise, they are PERFECT. They steam VERY easily when hung (a problem with a lot of thicker backdrops), are super soft and gorgeous when hung.

The only other problem I have with them is that the last one of five I have ordered came stained in several areas--and it's stained with something grey-tan that neither washes or even bleaches out. So...it's going back.

Still, all in all, these are SUCH a find for the price! If I decide to get more to use as a photo backdrop, I'd get two and layer them, because just one will likely show whatever is behind it, and they would also easily show tension if you try to place anything like a chair or other prop on them.

text_fidelity_a: VIZIO M70-C3 70-Inch Class Ultra HD Full-Array LED Smart TV I really like this TV. So why 4 stars instead of 5? I think back to the 42 inch Panasonic Plasma that I bought in 2002 and cringe at the multiple thousands spent. This is a lot of TV for the money. The picture is great. We have a 2012 59 inch top of the line Samsung Plasma and the picture on the Vizio is quite a bit sharper and brighter. It has replaced the Samsung as our go to Blue Ray movie night TV. So to this point we have a TV that is well priced and provides a great picture. So lets move on to the bad. Viewing angle. In our living room a couch sits directly in front of the Vizio. From the couch the picture is AMAZING. Off at about a 35 degree angle sits a recliner and the picture loses a lot of color, brightness and sharpness as viewed from the chair. It is not a horrible picture from the chair but it is quite a difference from straight on. The other is the somewhat slow response from the Vizio smart TV system. Compared to hooking up a Roku the initial start up and response is much slower. Of course if you are going to hook up a Roku then this is no big deal. If you do not have viewing angle concerns and are hooking up a Roku then I think you will absolutely love this amazing bargain.

Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones ...and after 13 years of heavy use, I was curious... here's my old headphones!

I went looking, because I like them so much all this time!

A couple things.

The mesh head thing- it only stayed on a couple years. They headphones worked better without it anyhow I think. Smoother on my hair. Which has a fine texture, and is a bit frizzy- lots of fine short pieces. Sometimes the foldable joints catch in them. This happens on earrings, necklaces, other headphones and other things as well. No more on this product really. Function of having fine curly hair.

Sound has always been fantastic. I love the sound and am sad when I send a ton of cash on headphones that don't come close.

They are not a snug fit, but, are soft enough and comfy enough to wear to bed. Because of the tender fabric, it's started to deteriorate on the smooth fake leathery bits. So so soft all this time though. Really to last 13 years, NO COMPLAINTS!!!.

Not snug enough to work out in. Snug enough to casually hike or walk in. They won't just fall right off or anything.

Lightweight. Easy to make a pouch or toss them into a ziplock freezer quart bag to travel and keep them in your pack or bag more tidily.

I would agree with most reviews. I tend to consider the cables 'supple' instead of 'flimsy'-- and this is an important difference! Supple cables don't just out at awkward angles and get caught on as much stuff. You can keep your music device in your pocket and the cable stays nicely under your coat or shirt and bends where you need it to stay and likes being there rather than tugging intself back in to the shape it wants to be in like a stiffer cable.

These are one of the few products I would give 10 stars to if I could.

And I still would after 13 years!!!!!!

Oh,

Actually they still work fine too. Really. I just noticed they are really a little fiddly nowadays because I used them so much, and was wondering if they still made them.

I have only had this for a day so I have not explored everything. This is my first tablet so I have little to compare it to, but I have a Kindle e-reader which I love. I found this to be pretty user friendly considering I don't even have a smartphone so apps and touchscreens are new to me. I found the user's guide to me helpful as well as the Kindle forum to answer questions I didn't feel like looking for answers to. I had no problem uploading my favorite sites. Some said they couldn't watch movies but I have been able to with both Netflix and Amazon on demand.Also, I guess there were some issues with the sound in the first generation Fire. I didn't have any problems, I didn't even need to use full volume when watching shows.
I downloaded a few free apps to play around with. And of course my books. I like that I can download some to the Fire but if there is one I want to read that I already own, I can download it from kindle Cloud. I can read books without downloading them via the Cloud but that means keeping the wireless on. Same with music.
I'm not to great with touchscreens and I loathe fingerprints so I prefer to use the stylus that I got separately. I didn't get a charger (it comes with USB cord only but charging through the computer won't really work), the one for my Kindle fits but doesn't charge as fast. So I ended up ordering the fast charger as the Fire isn't meant to last as many hours as the Kindle e-reader. But I still think the battery life is pretty good.
I like reading on this, I thought the back-light would bother me, but I can adjust the brightness. I actually prefer reading in the portrait mode as it shows two pages and looks like a book page would.
So far I am very happy with this, my third Kindle device. I like Amazon and find them to be very user friendly when I need help so I have no concerns so far. If there are any issues, I will update my review because I take spending my money very seriously.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd)

text_fidelity_a:
All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free] I've used glass screen protectors on several smartphones and digital cameras. This is my first time trying a large glass screen protector on a tablet. The kit contains everything you need, including a alcohol towel for cleaning your tablet (and your fingers), a sticker that tries to pick up all the lint on the tablet and the screen protector, and various other things that are less necessary. The glass is fine. It is slightly smaller than the Fire 8's screen (so you have some leeway if you don't install it perfectly). There is a little hole at the top so it doesn't cover the selfie camera. Honestly, I haven't noticed much difference between different brands of screen protectors.

If you've never installed a glass screen protector before, look on YouTube for tutorials. All of the similar products are installed the same way. You need to be really careful when installing this thing since it is large and difficult to align with your tablet's screen. I suggest that you try to align one edge of the protector as well as the camera hole and then hope for the best with the other edges. Make sure you pick up all the lint on both the tablet screen and the back of the screen protector, since any stray dust or lint is going to be noticeably ugly for as long as you have the screen protector installed. If you try to remove the screen protector to wipe off some lint that you missed, I guarantee that more lint will sucked in and make the problem worse, so you're best off doing a very thorough cleaning job the first time.

Whether or not you actually need a screen protector is a good question. If you use a case with a cover, then your chance of scratching the screen is small. I guess that depends on how rough you are with your tablet. You can go by your experience with other devices. A tablet is not like a smartphone that is sitting in your pocket with loose change and keys.
text_fidelity_b: All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free]

LG 32GK850G-B 32" QHD Gaming Monitor with 144Hz Refresh Rate and NVIDIA G-Sync,Black Amazing monitor...

At 3000:1 the contrast is very nice and better than most at this price range, and essentially all TN/IPS.

This is why I like VA panels, the black levels and the contrast. I've always bought IPS before and they're still great obviously, but after having a VA television, I started to personally prefer its benefits. There are obviously a few downsides when it comes to VA monitors, but this particular model solves most of them.

I have 2 IPS displays on both sides of this, and I can tell you the colors look excellent. It was also close to perfect calibration right out of the box, which was a nice change.

One review mentioned Gamma Mode 1 as closer to 2.2, but another comment mentioned Gamma Mode 3. Mode 3 seemed closest to me when calibrating, so I would recommend it.

Viewing angles:

The viewing angles aren't very good, as expected, but it doesn't affect me as I'm always right in front of my monitors. There is some slight vignetting when sitting close, so a curved screen could have been nice if implemented well.

Backlight bleed:

Having no IPS glow or backlight bleed is another benefit. With larger VA tvs there can occasionally be some slight blobbiness when in very dark settings, but this panel is very uniform with no BLB that I can see.

Size/pixel density:

I personally love bigger monitors, and don't have an issue with the pixel density here. Some people who are more sensitive to that might not be completely satisfied, but I personally would choose the increased immersion of a larger panel. Regardless, 1440p is awesome.

Ghosting/input lag:

In terms of ghosting, it's surprisingly almost nonexistent. Here's some comments from other people:

"I played some Doom last night, and literally did nothing but rapidly move my camera all over the place to see if I could notice any ghosting or bleeding. I couldn't find anything objectionable..."

"Also there is very little ghosting in the monitor which is super rare for VA panels."

"...even in dark games like Outlast 2/Doom, the ghosting is so hard to see that you have to intentionally find a worst case scenario to try and induce it."

"Ghosting is slight, about on par with 165 Hz IPS gaming panels from my testing. Only TN is faster really."

In terms of input lag, tftcentral says: "We measured a total display lag of only 6.40ms. With approximately 4.15ms of that accounted for by pixel response times we had an estimated signal processing of just 2.25ms, which was next to nothing. This is in keeping with other G-sync screens we have tested, as the absence of an additional scaler (and presence of the G-sync module) allows for extremely low lag."

This monitor is exactly what I've been waiting for. The circular light bar on the back is a nice touch as well, although it could be a bit brighter. I also would have preferred a sharpness slider, but it's not entirely necessary.

FYI, it can be freely moved in basically every direction, including 90 degree rotation - if you need that for some reason.

So if you don't have issues with viewing angles/slightly higher pixel density, this is an excellent choice as it excels in basically every other area.
text_fidelity_b: LG 32GK850G-B 32" QHD Gaming Monitor with 144Hz Refresh Rate and NVIDIA G-Sync,Black

Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding I'm having a serious problem with the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base that apparently the other reviewers are not having. I called Denon Technical Support and after spending a lot of time behind the TV set making sure all the wires were hooked up correctly and then pressing different buttons on the Denon Speaker base, they can't figure out what is causing this problem. And the problem is this: No sound signal is going to the Denon speaker base through the TV from the Roku player. The Roku works just fine through the regular TV speakers and is connected directly to the TV via HDMI. When the input on the TV is set to stream via the Roku no sound comes through the Denon and it turns off. If I increase the volume on the TV speakers you hear sound. If the input is changed to TV with the TV sound off, sound will come through the Denon. Also, if a DVD is played on the DVD player which is connected to the TV, the sound comes through the Denon. It just won't put out sound when the Roku input is being used. And that's a real bummer for me because we watch a lot of Netflix and Amazon streaming through our Roku. I am using the digital optical cord included with the Denon Speaker Base. I have it connected to the Digital Optical "Out" on the back of my Sharp 37" flat screen TV to the digital optical "In" on the back of the Denon Speaker Base.

I will keep working on this problem, and if anyone reading this has any idea that might fix it please say so in the comments section. I would love very much to have it work and to raise the star level to 5. When sound does come through the Denon it's great! Loud, clear and no buzzes or rattles whatsoever like when the volume is turned all the way up when using the TV speakers. I love that it can get loud and there's no rattles or weird vibrations. and the night mode is very useful since the TV room is located underneath the main bedroom and my husband has to go to bed early since he has to go to work early. I like to stay up late and watch Netflix/Amazon or other streaming channels through the Roku (oops! That doesn't work through the Denon) and I keep the volume down lest it wake him up. I was really looking forward to using the Denon night sound function.

The Denon tech suggested hooking everything up to another TV to see if the problem is the Roku player or my TV. Unfortunately, I don't have another TV to test out the units to try and isolate the lack of sound from the Roku player to the Denon. I was really wanting to use this for night listening, but since I can't I will take the Denon to my mom's nursing home and hook it up to her small, flat-screen TV. Since she's half deaf, it might can help her hear the sound better. I will update this review afterwards.
text_fidelity_b: Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding

text_fidelity_a:
Onkyo HT-S5100 7.1 Channel Home Entertainment System (Set of Nine, Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The Onkyo HT-S5100 Home Entertainment System sounded quite good when listening to the radio, and I really loved the self-calibration feature to set the speaker phase/power-level based upon our optimum seating position.

When the receiver is played at low to mid volume ranges, the system was impressive, but there was distoration at higher levels when the speakers were driven beyond their capabilities.

As far as a Stereo Receiver goes, I'd give it high marks, but as far as a Home Entertainment system goes... in my opinion, I'd purchase something else.

I found after many frustrating hours of trying to get the receiver to work with my other HDMI components, that all of my attempts were in vain.

I'd essentially purchased the system on the recommedation of Consumer Reports (They crowed about the HT-S5100 having the best sound of any system they'd ever tested, and it was one of the only ones offering 7.1 versus 5.1 stereo surround).

I eventually re-read the Onkyo Owners Manual and found a small blurb regarding the audio of the system not working with HDMI...

I freely admit I'd blown-off the fact that analog/digital connectors were shown on the Quick Hook-Up illustrations (thinking these were alternative connections for those unlucky soul's who didn't have HDMI), when I finally resorted to contacting Onkyo for assistance/confirmation.

They confirmed my worst-fear, their HDMI's were (Pass-Though). When asked why they even bothered to put HDMI connectors on the system, the reply was (some consumers desired them).

Personally, I feel if a system has HDMI connectors present, that is implies they're fully compliant, otherwise their presence is misleading.

What this meant was all of my new toy's (50" Plasma, Blu-ray player, and Xbox 360) could only pass on video (not the higher quality audio signals through the HDMI connectors), and that I'd have to accept a lower quality audio output due to the use of standard audio connectors.

Perhaps I'd missed this in CR's review (or it wasn't stated), as I had to purchase additional digital cabling so that I could even hear the audio content of the devices hooked into the Onkyo (added expense/wiring woe's).

If I had to do it all over again, I'd purchase the HT-S5100 as a Stereo Receiver, but I wouldn't recommend it as the hub for a Home Entertainment System to interconnect your HDMI devices.

Another pearl-of-wisdom, don't rely strictly upon the written advice of a third-party, go out and listen/view the equipment yourself, as that's what I'm wishing I'd have done!
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo HT-S5100 7.1 Channel Home Entertainment System (Set of Nine, Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only I really bought a Canon DSLR (vs Nikon, or any of the mirrorless Cameras) for this lens. I needed a low distortion very wide lens for real estate videos and I also needed image stabilization and quiet focusing. I don't think there is any other lens from any manufacturer that satisfies all of those things except this one. (Sigma has the 10-20mm but no stabilization, lower optical quality, and more money! Tamaron - 10-24 - same story. And so on ).
GOOD: Excellent optical quality for the price. This lens is noticeably sharper and has less distortion at 10mm than my kit lens 18-135mm has at 18mm. Stabilization works very well. Focusing is very fast and silent. I don't hear it even with the built in mic when shooting video (on a Canon 70D). Extremely lightweight and fairly compact.

BAD: Maximum Aperture. This is NOT a fast lens. F/4.5 maximum is not that great and you lose it pretty quickly as you zoom in since the max aperture ranges from 4.5 - 5.6. You need to have some decent light to shoot with this lens. But given the lack of competition in super wide stabilized silent EF-S lenses (or any Canon mount lens) and the price of anything vaguely similar, I think it's a reasonable compromise.

Note: At this price, you can't really call it a knock, but it'd be nice if it came with the lens hood. You can get a clone lens hood for $10 or so.

ALSO: Canon has now updated their EOS Utility software for this lens.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player (Black) SanDisk has come out with an extension to their array of MP3 players, beyond the Clip and the View. Their new mp3 player, the Sansa Fuze, is definitely geared towards casual someone who just wants a basic, functional, and well-put together media device for their pocket.

The Sansa Fuze may look like a tiny device at first, but this thing packs some serious features. It has the ability to playback music, video, photos, FM radio, as well as audiobooks. The features for the Sansa Fuze are very impressive to say the least, as it also features a microSD card slot to add extra storage space, content, etc.

The first feature we will focus on is the one which will likely get the most use, the audio aspect. The music menu is organized with artist, album, song, genre, etc. There is also a recently added section which shows the most recent songs added onto the device, as well as a top rated section.

The album menu allows you to see album icons as you are scrolling through the various albums. There is also the ability to form a playlist directly on the player.

The sound quality is very well-done. If you have a great set of headphones you will not be disappointed in the least bit.

The video aspect is definitely not the highlight of the Sansa Fuze. Part of this is due to the low power of the device, and partly due to the screen itself. The supplied Sansa Media Converter does make it easy to convert movies into a format for the device though. A typical movie will take up a little under, or over 1GB. The video looks respectable, but can get a bit choppy at times. One very cool feature about the video is the ability to add a bookmark while watching it.

The photo viewer is very standard as you can view photos from the internal memory of a microSD card. You can set up a slide show with time intervals, and add music as well. The images looked quite sharp.

The FM radio feature is done extremely well on the Sansa Fuze. You get some great reception and the auto program feature picks out crystal clear radio stations. It also has the ability to record radio in WAV format.

This works with voice recording as well thanks to a microphone located right below the microSD slot.

Podcasts and audiobooks are pretty self-explanatory, but one issue with the audiobooks is the lack of a bookmark feature.

The overall user interface for the Sansa Fuze is put together nicely, set up in such a way that a first-time user could pick up this device and feel right at home with it. You have a scroll wheel as well as a home button and a middle click wheel. The scroll wheel can also be clicked up and down, which can make things a bit confusing at times. Overall though, beyond a few hiccups with organizational aspects of the UI, this is one easy device to use.

Getting media onto the Sansa Fuze is extremely simple as you can use any desktop media player to create playlists and such, easily syncing them to the device. It also supports drag and drop without the need for any software. We used Windows Media Player as well as a few other media players to test this all out, and syncing was as simple as can be.

The quality of the device itself is top-notch, as the screen can put out some great contrast and vibrant colors in spots. The screen is extremely clear and does a nice job with photo presentations. Battery life is equally as impressive, as I have been getting around 20 hours on each battery charge thus far. Video playback came in at around 6 hours on a charge.

The package comes with a proprietary USB cable and a pair of earbuds, pretty basic.

Also shipping with the Sansa Fuze is a great bonus, a microSD card which comes with DRM-free music from more than 50 new and emerging artists. This is a great way to immediately test out the music capabilities of the Sansa Fuze, and also adds value to the entire package. Music videos, images, and more are also included on the microSD card.

Overall SanDisk has done a great job with the Sansa Fuze.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player (Black)

Armor Suit MilitaryShield Screen Protector For Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 10.1 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film I bought this to keep the screen of my roughly $300 tablet safe from scratches. I watched the YouTube instruction video as the included instruction sheet asked. It took me two tries to put the screen on how I wanted it. By that time I had used almost all of the solution. I put the tablet on a dry, dust-free level surface and left it alone for over 24 hours, as instructed.

The screen protector doesn't quite fit the screen (and yes, I bought the correct shield for my tablet). There is a small portion on the left side of the screen that is not covered because the shield is all the way to the right edge of the screen. It has been three days and there are still bubbles under the shield, which makes me think I must have not pushed all the moisture out. The instructions said any imperfections such as micro-bubbles would go away on their own after a couple days. I guess I will see if they do.

The tablet still responds to touching with my fingertips with the shield on. I did notice that when I was using the tablet after installing the shield and waiting the specified time for it to dry that it was difficult to remove little bits and pieces of whatever debris from the environment falls on the screen. Wiping it away takes more effort because things seem to stick to the shield.

That said, I will say that the company seems to pride itself on service, which I appreciate. They include a quality microfiber cloth and a little plastic wedge (I don't know how else to describe it) to push bubbles and moisture from under the shield after it is applied, and the solution is in a quality thin, plastic spray bottle. They also really want feedback so it seems they are committed to improving their service. My rating is for the actual product, the installation required, and overall look, not the company itself.

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix T300 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens (Black) For the non-professional photographer looking to get high-quality images in a variety of settings, this camera works great. I did a little experiment to see how it performed by taking it with me to Europe along with a much more expensive semi-professional Nikon (D3100). Here are the results:

Advantages:
-With our limited time, my camera was able to take a variety of shots (panoramic, zoom, close-up) quickly and easily while the Nikon could only take limited kinds because of the need to bring several lenses and because of the complexity (sometimes) of setting up a given shot
-Because it was small, I didn't have to lug around a big camera bag, which also had the potential of getting a little too much unwanted attention
-One feature I really enjoyed was the two simultaneous flash/no flash shot which gives you the same picture with and without flash, letting you choose later which you prefer
-Didn't need more than one lens
-With city shots of architecture, my camera fared better with its versatility

Disadvantages:
-In the mountains, the Nikon did better, capturing color and clarity/detail. In my shots, the trees looked less defined from high up. Also, his zoom lens was able to capture much more detail than my camera.
-Nature shots and portraits have slightly duller colors, missing something the other camera was able to capture
-There was slightly more blur in shots with movement with this camera

Conclusion:
For the price, this camera performed much better than I expected and was not as much of a hassle as our semi-professional camera, so for most people, this is not only going to be a better value, but less frustrating and cumbersome. For the professional, this is obviously not the best choice, but this isn't being marketed as a professional camera. This is a great family and vacation camera that everyone can use, and that still yields quality images with plenty of artistic integrity.
Great little camera, and fun to use!

**see pics for some examples of how this camera performed**

Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player (Old Model) I've been thinking about getting a Roku for some time, so when it was a Gold Box deal I took the plunge. I'm now kicking myself for not buying it sooner - this is great! Rather than be limited to streaming on my laptop, I can now stream from Amazon Prime and Netflix on the TV, plus have the sound routed through my home theater setup.

Setup of the Roku was about as simple as could be. I was up and running in less than 30 minutes, with a large portion of that time spent downloading updates or figuring out how to route the cables so they would not appear as attractive playthings for the cats. I hardwired this into my router rather than go wireless since the router is just a few feet away from the player.

I hooked the HDMI cable into my home theater receiver. I really can't tell the difference between streaming and playing a Blu-ray or DVD in terms of sound or video quality. My internet connection is 30Mbps.

I was surprised at how small the box is. Just a few inches wide and about an inch or so thick. I think the HDMI cable weighs more than the actual device. Very easy to find a spot to put it.

The remote is OK. I wish the buttons were a bit larger and/or were backlit so you can see them in a darkened room. It's usable and functional, but pretty basic.

Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player (Old Model)

Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design. This is a very basic keyboard, but it gets nearly everything right. The layout adheres to the QUERTY convention, it has illuminated indicators for caps and num lock, it has a numeric keypad, and basic multimedia controls (play/pause and volume). It covers all of the bases for a basic keyboard.

The key feel is nice. It's quiet, and the keys are comfortable to press. The function keys are smaller than the other keys to save on space but work just fine. The attached USB cord is nice and long (about 6 foot). The overall build quality feels decently solid for the price point. It auto installed on Win 10 without a hitch.

Misses are minor. It lacks a sleep button. It has a calculator button instead that, for me, is far less useful than a sleep button. It also lacks non-slip pads on the base. There are two legs that can be used to prop up the keyboard, but the keyboard is so light that it's easy to shift the position of it in use. I solved it with some stick-on non-slip material.

I've always used Microsoft keyboards and have yet to have one fail on me. There are other basic keyboards that are a dollar or two less expensive than this, but considering this is less than $11, I'd rate the overall value as very good. If you're looking for a basic, everyday keyboard and don't need/want anything fancy, this will fit the bill well and do so at a great price. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design.

I would not buy this again. Look to the real brands like linksys, Nest, Ring, etc. if you actually want a security camera and not a little toy.

The two reasons I went for this activity tracker are it is waterproof and the battery lasts one year... for me these are the most important reasons because I really hate all this constant charging of gadgets.

Syncing is easy, at the end of the day I just press one button and it syncs with my smartphone, it also comes with a little blue-tooth USB attachment if you want to sync it with your computer. I've read they will add autosync with the next software update which is supposed to arrive shortly.

You get to choose what to see on your screen when you press the button, I went with steps, goal, distance and time. You can also add the date, calories and heart rate if you are wearing a strap.

I absolutely love how it feels, it doesn't bother me at all, you don't have to wear it real tight and the silicon is very soft.

The reason I took one star off is that the beep sound which comes on after one hour of inactivity (when the red warning line appears) is way, way, way too quiet. I set an alarm just to check on the beep sound and it was so short and subtle, if there would be any kind of background noise you won't be able to hear it at all.

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth Let's do the pro/con thing.

Pros:

+ Sound is definitely amazing coming from 1 amp @ 5 volts. I wouldn't have guessed that was quite possible. And the stereo effect works well, especially if you're positioned indirectly to the speaker (i.e., not right beside it). That said, it's not an amazing amount better than the SBX8, so I wonder if the (untested by me) SBX10 would be the sweet spot in terms of size to sound ratio.

+ Integrated microphone features work well, although I'm still not sold on voice commands.

+ Bluetooth combined with direct AC power option makes it truly versatile.

+ This would be awesome to have as the communications centerpiece in a temporary apartment while on the road, to use in any room that doesn't have speakers, or even as a centerpiece in a smaller apartment. That said, it's a bit large to want to travel on planes with, but I would do it for a long trip.

+ As long as you're getting your power via an electrical outlet (and NOT a computer, although as an "ejected" (from the computer) device, it should work as well), you are able to communicate to the speaker with bluetooth and with the line in jack, which allows this to be a more permanent fixture. You can have it work with your phone and still be hooked up to a more permanent sound source. In fact, the speaker will play two sources at once in that case, but a full USB connection to a computer shuts it off to the rest of the world (i.e., in that case, it will ignore the line in and the bluetooth connections.

+ Cool capacitive touch controls.

Cons:

- No way to shut it off short of unplugging. This makes a more permanent setup less attractive. Not that it's eating much power just sitting there, but still...

- Included (thankfully) AC adapter could be smaller and shaped more efficiently. It comes with plugs for US, Continental Europe, UK, and Australia (which covers most of the world since most countries use one of those), but the latter two hang off the front of the unit awkwardly. You couldn't plug it in beside most AC adapters. Anyway, most people have some other ones sitting around if this one is not adequate.

- My BB - although it recognizes the device as a SoundBlaster SBX20, not generically - cannot control the volume like a bluetooth headset I use. This must be done from the integrated controls.

- I have to reinitiate bluetooth connection from my phone (thankfully not from the unit) after each power down. Actually not sure if this is a pro or a con...depends on your thinking.

In summary, this is a really cool, versatile device with a lot of interesting features. It is a niche, however. I'd call it just about perfect for someone on a long term assignment away from home and perfect for some people as an in-house permanent setup, although the lack of a power switch bothers me for those uses. It's a bit large for short term travel unless by personal vehicle. Hopefully this helps you decide if this is right for you.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth

text_fidelity_a:
Bose CineMate 1 SR Home Theater Speaker System (Black) I bought this system to replace my Yamaha YSP-500 and a fairly sizeable subwoofer. My issue was that we were doing a remodel of our living room to put in a wall with a fireplace and stonework where our existing entertainment center was. Because the Yamaha projector is fairly substantial, mounting it directly to the wall wasn't an option, so I would have had to build another shelf or do something else. I would have also had to relocate the sub which would have meant either buying some sort of wireless set up or running a cable under the floor and into the wall.

Since the Bose speaker is much slimmer and lighter, has an available wall bracket, and the sub is wireless I thought I had the solution to my problem. For that part, the Bose is great. It was easy to mount, is relatively unobtrusive, and having more flexibility with the placement of the sub is really nice. If you have space limitations or just don't want to mess with running speaker wire (or can't) then this is a good alternative.

This is also a good alternative for people that just want to plug something in and have it work. If you are technically challenged, or just don't want to invest the time in setting up a home theater then this is a usable solution. Most people could have this up and running (including configuration) in less than 20 minutes.

I thought the sound quality is pretty decent. I don't know that it is significantly better than the older (and cheaper) Yamaha Sound Projector that it replaced. Unlike some reviewers, I thought voices (at least on television shows) were clearer and easier to hear than what I was used to. The bass was crisp, but I haven't experienced the punch I am used to with my Yamaha sub. Granted the Bose Accoustimass module is a lot smaller, but there is a very noticeable difference.

There are two areas that I took a star away for each. One is obviously cost. At around $1000, I would say that this would be a better value. At its current price I think that you are not really getting what you pay for. For all the trade-offs, I think there are cheaper alternatives.

The second is the fact that it lacks any sort of display or ability to customize. You can't make any sort of sound profiles (movies, sports, etc), you don't have anything like a night mode, and there is no display whatsoever to indicate something as simple as volume level. Some people may like that, but to me it was rather annoying. For the price, I think you should be able to do a little more with it. Again, if you are the plug-and-play type, this probably won't bother you.

Overall, other than the size and wireless sub, this is not an improvement from my Yamaha Sound Projector. I think it's good, but if I had to do it over again I would probably look at other, cheaper options.
text_fidelity_b: Bose CineMate 1 SR Home Theater Speaker System (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This little device came in handy during my recent trip to San Francisco, CA. I connected my Garmin nüvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator to my Toyota and it worked great. Installing and using this little machine is simple and easy. The instructions are easy to follow. I had a great time going to different places in San Francisco using this GPS and it never failed me. If you take a wrong route or direction, no problem, it will re-calculate and give the directions to get back on the right tack and keep driving. It works wonderfully. This has many features to help you get from point A to point B quickly and safely; features such as audible driving directions with text-to-speech (TTS), spoken street names, real-time traffic updates, and Internet connectivity for points-of-interest search, 5-inch resistive touch screen with colorful, animated map graphics and large easy-to-read screens are some of the coolest features. It comes complete with free lifetime map updates and traffic reports. The traffic reports are indicated pictorially using specific colors; red (heavy traffic), green (easy traffic) and yellow (moderate traffic). You do get a 3D junction view and speed limit indicators. If you are driving over the speed limit, the speed limit (e.g. 65 MPH), the display of 65 MPH goes red, if you are below the speed limit, it goes green.

It also offer robust point-of-interest (POI) search, including good category breakdowns, as well as searches that update in real time as you drive, complete with compass directions. When we were in Berkeley, CA, we were in an area which was completely new to us, and we wanted to go to an Indian restaurant and this feature helped us to find the nearest restaurant.

My brother uses GPS-enabled smart-phones and recommended me to go for GPS and I have never regretted buying this little gizmo, this offers good value for money.

Pros
* Big 5-inch screen
* Free lifetime traffic
* Pedestrian/public transit navigation
* Multi-destination routing
* Lane assist

Cons
* We had routing problems in some cases. It did not give the correct straight forward directions in my own home town. Once the satellite communication did not work when we are going to the airport.
* Traffic/lane info is available only in some cities
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
SmartDelux 13-Port Powered USB Hub = 10 USB 3.0 Data + 3 Charging Ports for PC & Laptop, 5ft PA Cord UPDATE (5/19/2019):
Today my external hard drive is not recognized when it is plugged into this hub. I am NOT restarting my computer to test whether it is necessary to have the HDD recognized. It IS recognized when it is plugged into a different hub that is also plugged into my Mac mini.

Since my 4-bay HDD enclosure has to remain connected for the hourly Time Machine backups, it is now connected directly to my Mac mini. The only reason to keep this hub is for charging any device.

UPDATE (2/15/2019):
Other drives (SSD and HDD) that were connected to this hub also disconnected themselves. The wired Apple aluminum keyboard (it came with my 2008 Mac Pro) is plugged into this hub, and it does not generate the warning that the device was disconnected. If I were shopping for a USB hub, I would stay away from this one. Nothing is "deluxe" except the name - and the lighted ports.

UPDATE (2/9/2019):
My devices - SSDs and 4-bay HDD enclosure - that are plugged into this hub have been disconnecting for no apparent reason. I thought my Logitech mouse was disconnecting because the dongle was plugged into it, but that seems to be the fault of the dongle since it continued while plugged into my keyboard. I have moved my keyboard cable to the hub, and we will see how long that lasts. The 4-bay enclosure is more critical, so it is connected to a USB port on my computer. When the enclosure was connected to this hub, I kept seeing that warning that my drives were Not Ejected Properly

Connected this to my computer's USB 3.0 port. Plugged in the dongle for my battery powered mouse. Mouse began acting erratically, had to remove the dongle and reinsert it to reconnect. Functioned properly for a short while but disconnected.
Finally had to plug dongle in the port on my wired keyboard before it would stay connected and not perform erratically. Something must be interrupting the signal even when the LEDs indicate the hub is connected even during periods when my computer is asleep.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (1/25/2019):
The hub has 3 smart charging ports, but when viewed from an angle, only the two on the end have orange / red LED light showing - the 3rd one appears blue. All lights are bright - brighter than they need to be.

A 4-bay HDD enclosure is plugged into this hub and has been functioning without any problem for the 2 weeks I have had the enclosure connected. Connecting an SSD through this hub also functions with no problem using a SATA-USB3 cable.

Yes, of course you could use the wall, a bed sheet or some other improvised backdrop, but it would defeat the whole point of seeing a film in the manner this projector was designed for.

And between you and me, I'm not that excited watching the NASA channel nonstop. You could use your Prime membership to watch movies, but that wasn't so great either.

Other reviewers have suggested it would be terrific for a slumber party. Really? What's the matter with your big screen T.V.? The picture quality is excellent but the sound is not up to par. If you're gonna go this far then you really need to be firing on all cylinders with the sound and the picture.

In conclusion, this is really a disappointment. I had hoped I could watch baseball or something else of interest to me, but this projector requires too many variables to line up perfectly, and it's just not worth the time or the effort.

The one positive - it's really cute and small.

text_fidelity_a:
Yamaha AVENTAGE RX-A880 7.2-ch 4K Ultra HD AV Receiver with HDR Dolby Vision Dolby Atmos Wi-Fi Phono YPAO and MusicCast. Works with Alexa. Update: I really love this machine. You give a lot of things five stars if they're really good products, but this one deserves bonus. I've been slowly going through the full 200+ page manual to make sure I don't miss any features and to get the most out of this thing, and I'm continually thrilled. Also, I give a lot of things controlled by apps low ratings because I tend to hate screwing around with my phone, but in this case, the Yamaha AV controller app only adds to the value, with the best part being you don't NEED it to take advantage of all the receiver's functionality, but it's a joy to have sometimes to make fine adjustments without having to turn on the TV. I really like it for adjusting net radio stations and stuff like that or fine tuning music sounds - again, without having to turn on the TV. This also makes up for the one negative I mentioned below about not being able to change all the settings from a web page. Great stuff!

Original review:

Before this, I had two Sony receivers in my living room. My secondary is a much older model - about 12 or so years old - that does not have HDMI and I use it for my whole house audio system. My primary is (was - it just got replaced) a 3-5 year old Sony model that is admittedly in a lower class than this Yamaha receiver (the secondary was in a higher class in its time, I think).

While I usually have all Sony stuff, I was completely willing to try another well-known Japanese brand who specializes in receivers and amps. And - it's just awesome. Totally. Not a single regret about the switch. The RX-A880 gave me back everything I lost going from my older, higher-end Sony to my newer one, AND it gave me so many nice surprises on the way! As anyone can tell you that it sounds good and looks good, I'll concentrate on this little details that I discovered during setup:

1) Besides the seven HDMI inputs, it also has a composite video, a component video, two optical audio, one extra (second belongs to component) coax audio, and two composite audio inputs, not to mention phono.

The great thing is that you can assign different audio inputs to any of the video inputs. So, for example, I decided to keep my Wii around since I now have a component input (and it takes up almost no space), but the cable is component video with composite audio, but the component video input on this has coax for the audio. Bummer. But no, you can change it. Example number two is I have a computer in my telecom closet hooked up to this with both HDMI and line-out audio. For circumstances too complicated to define here, audio does not output via the HDMI. But because of this feature, I can make the audio appear when I select the HDMI input OR when I just want to listen to the audio directly (with no HDMI output). Perfect.

2) 9 Speaker outputs. First, I'm so happy to have the 2-zone thing back (my secondary receiver has it, but my other, newer Sony did not - it only had A/B speakers that shared an amp). But this one you can actually have 7.1 AND a second zone (although you can't play them at the same time. This is really cool if you want the best of both worlds. I don't know if I can find a place for two more speakers in my setup, but ...it's nice to have the option. Supposedly, this all works automatically. I imagine it could work fine, but I am unable to try it at the moment.

3) 2-zone done better. My older Sony had 2-zone, but the controls were - frankly - atrocious. It was always confusing, even for someone like me who can be a super A/V nerd and memorize anything. The way I use it now is just to keep the remote on Zone-2, and do Zone-1 on the unit itself.

This Yamaha, however, has a simple switch on the remote, and you're either controlling one zone or the other depending on that switch. Simple and effective. You can also control it from the unit, unlike the older Sony.

4) 8 custom presets, all controlled directly from the remote. Another 8 for Zone 2?!

The one complaint I read by a reviewer was that you have to scroll through all the inputs from the remote to get to what you want. But that doesn't matter for two reasons: first, you can change the settings to skip anything you don't want. But, second, with 8 custom presets - and each with their own remote button - you probably don't even ever need to scroll through the inputs anyway.

And the custom presets are great. You can turn on and off a bunch of features like whether or not it changes your HDMI out settings, if it uses your YPAO settings, extra bass, which speakers it uses, etc. And it even can link the second zone!

Two great examples:

I can't stand to watch regular background TV with the surround sound on because it makes the commercials that much more obnoxious. But of course I like big booming bass and surround for movies. And it's also annoying to switch the unit off and on all the time, especially if you want to use control for HDMI. So I have one preset for very flat TV sound using just the front speakers that is clearer than-, but no more annoying than-, my regular TV speakers. Then I have another preset for surround sound and big bass for movie watching.

I have one preset for straight music just in zone 1. Then I have another preset for straight music in both zones one and two. It turns on zone 2 automatically. I could not figure out how to make a preset just for zone 2, but it seems that when I am controlling zone 2 on the remote, I can make 8 more presets just for zone 2. You can not adjust these presets via menu, from what I can tell, though.

5) 14 character names on the front of the unit in dot matrix. My other receivers were all limited to 8 characters. You can see all 14 at once, which is great.

6) Much more robust networking. I haven't played with this too awful much yet, but it seems that if you start listening to a playlist or an album on your NAS, then the next time you go back to "server", it will start playing where you left off (well, the song you left off at will start over again, instead of at the exact moment you left at), but at least this way you don't have to turn the TV on just to play some music. I suppose you could create a playlist of all Death Metal, and then you just have a stream going whenever you want it. It also seems like you can actually sign into Pandora and all the other stations and listen to your own account. And all the Internet/Network stuff is a separate scroll-through than the other inputs. I really like how that is set up.

6) The "program up/down" buttons on the remote can be programmed to do about 10 different things. I picked to have the dialogue increased or decreased for when you can't hear what people are saying even though everything else is loud enough. To be clear, I think this depends on if the dialogue is known to the decoder. I haven't tried all the other options yet.

7) Remote is awesome. Besides what I mentioned above, you can also make some changes to the red/green/yellow/blue buttons, but I wish you could really program those completely to your liking. Everything is laid out nicely, and the second zone even makes sense, as I mentioned above.

8) I realize the second HDMI output would be great if you also have a projector or something like that. With it, you can have access to all your devices without having to rewire anything. Haven't used it yet, but am glad to have the extra functionality.

...

There's plenty more, but I'm forgetting some of the details right now. I've only played with this thing for a few days, but I like it more and more. The one thing that is missing is that you can't change all the options via the webpage. You can change some, but I liked with my newer Sony the fact that I could look at and change all my custom presets without having to turn the TV and go through all that. I'm only comparing this to my two Sony units so you get my frame of reference, but realize this Yamaha model is in a higher class than those. Regardless, I love this thing, and it has a lot of great functionality and no serious drawbacks that I've noticed yet. Recommended (obviously).
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha AVENTAGE RX-A880 7.2-ch 4K Ultra HD AV Receiver with HDR Dolby Vision Dolby Atmos Wi-Fi Phono YPAO and MusicCast. Works with Alexa.

text_fidelity_a: Pioneer Electronics Audition Series XW_NAS3-K Docking Station for iPod (Black) I was the happy owner of the original Bose sounddock for seven years until it stopped working this November.  I thought that was a very good run.  To replace the Bose I chose the Pioneer NAS3 and waited a month for the price to drop to $220.  I like the clean design as I wasn't looking for a display nor was I looking for an alarm clock.  On first play I was not at all impressed with the muddy flat sound until I found that under the music menu on the ipod is a setting for 'speakers'.  Going into 'speakers' I can enhance the sound with the bass/treble on setting which is comparable to the ipod EQ acoustic setting.  You can really bump up the sound by turning on both but for me the sound becomes unnaturally bright and the bass distorts.  In other words the dock does respond to all ipod EQ settings.  Under 'speakers' I can also set the ipod display to always be on, always be off, or only come on when I press a key on the dock or on the remote.  Speaking of the remote, the range is strangely bad as you need to point it almost directly at the unit.  To make the NAS bluetooth capable then you'll need to buy the adaptor separately.  I don't know if it's only the Pioneer adaptor that will work but if that's the case, it's a pricey option at about $70. If this were an issue for me I would have rated the Pioneer three stars.  The sound quality here just doesn't earn it a five-star rating but I'll be keeping the unit.  If I had it to do it over again I would go with another Bose.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Electronics Audition Series XW_NAS3-K Docking Station for iPod (Black)

Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth This SR-C20A is an entry-level Yamaha soundbar made for the smaller room and bedroom. The attraction to this model was the 3rd speaker, a powered subwoofer.

Most compact soundbars create bass through passive radiators integral with the bar … i.e. 2 powered speakers separated in width by a baffled tube radiating through holes. So, there is no controllable bass other than passive baffle sound effects.

The SR-C20A has a controllable powered subwoofer and a dual baffle radiator combined to deliver controllable high, medium, and low tones. There are five modes: standard, stereo, game, movie, and a virtual surround mode. I just picked the one that sounds best. The virtual surround provides a sense of depth and separation to my hearing.

The SR-C20A soundbar replaced a no-name 2-speaker with baffles. The difference is sizable sound improvement.

Easy install, lots of input options.

Better sound than expected. Impressive sound. Sized for the smaller room LCD/OLEAD TV. Priced right.
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth

StarTech.com 2.5in USB 3.0 SSD SATA Hard Drive Enclosure - Storage enclosure with power indicator - 2.5" - SATA 3Gb/s - 3 Gbit/s - USB 3.0 - black (SAT2510BU32) I'm using this enclosure for an earlier-gen SATA thin profile 500GB Western Digital hard drive and getting great results. The fastest removable media I own is a SanDisk Extreme USB 3.0 flash drive. And with this enclosure, the WD hard drive is hitting read/write speeds that are almost as fast as the SanDisk Extreme. It's not nearly SATA III fast (since it's not a SATA III drive), but fast.

I followed the recommendation of other reviewers and reformatted the hard drive to MBR and NTFS file system before using. This requires using DiskPart or Disk Management in Windows. Instructions are available on the web.

Older hard drives with a thick profile won't fit this enclosure. If you're not sure if your hard drive is thin profile and you don't have a metric ruler handy, if it's a quarter inch or less in thickness (and has a SATA connector) it's thin profile and will fit this enclosure.

I did not get good results testing the enclosure with a desktop computer with only USB 2.0 capability---it was very slow or not even recognized when plugged in. I don't want to blame the enclosure, because I've had similar issues with other brand enclosures and that same desktop computer. But I want to mention this in case you're thinking of buying this to use with a computer that only has USB 2.0. You might do better to get a USB 2.0 enclosure.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com 2.5in USB 3.0 SSD SATA Hard Drive Enclosure - Storage enclosure with power indicator - 2.5" - SATA 3Gb/s - 3 Gbit/s - USB 3.0 - black (SAT2510BU32)

text_fidelity_a: APC Surge Protector with Telephone, DSL and Coaxial Protection, P11VT3, 3020 Joules, 11 Outlet Surge Protector Power Strip Gray I have been using APC products professionally for years, as part of my job with FEMA. All of our computers, servers, modems, routers and printers are connected through APC UPS units with built in surge protectors, or units like this one,. FEMA goes into areas where storms happen frequently and with great ferocity. Power interruptions and surges are very common. A few months ago, we had an electrical storm in our area, lots of lighting and thunder. We took a pretty good hit somewhere near our house which knocked out power for a pretty large area, and caused some damage to the grid. But, when you need it, you need it and don't want to go to UPS store to fax a simple one page document. We did this for a while. But, finally, I broke down and got a new printer. So, this time, it's going to be well protected. As is everything else in my home network equipment. This APC unit protects ALL of the connections, phone, ethernet, coax AND electrical. It even comes with jumpers for all three data connections. $25 is a small price to pay, to protect over $2,000 worth of equipment. Oh, and just remember that most surge protectors have to be replaced like every three years. This one comes with a LIFETIME warranty with $1000 equipment replacement guarantee. So, good purchase. Five stars.

text_fidelity_a: Crucial MX500 1TB 3D NAND SATA 2.5 Inch Internal SSD, up to 560MB/s - CT1000MX500SSD1 I have always used HDD drives but have had 4 hard drive failures over the past 15 years and I was sick of it. Learning that an SSD drive is not subject to overheating like an HDD I switched over to this Crucial 500gb SSD. It was easy to clone the hard drive with the free Acronis download from Crucial. It took about 4 hours to clone the SSD then I took out the HDD and replaced it with the SSD in my laptop. That was relatively easy too. Now the good part. The SSD is lightening fast. My HDD took about 3 minutes to reboot the computer. This SSD takes about 20 seconds! I was amazed. Microsoft Word took 30-40 seconds to open with the HDD. It opens in 6 seconds with the SSD. Now my computer flys like speedy falcon instead of like a slow crow. I read that an SSD will last decades while an HDD lasts anywhere from 15 seconds to 5 years depending on the circumstances.  I am into having a computer be reliable and not breaking down. Like I said I have had 4 hard drives go kaput over the last 15 years or so. I have lost very important data (now I back up but still nice not to have to worry about HDD failure). Now I feel secure knowing that an SSD drive is likely to never break down, no data loss, no expensive repair bills or having to buy a new computer, and it should last a long time. I am so glad I bought this SSD and am very happy with it. I think it is a quality unit.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial MX500 1TB 3D NAND SATA 2.5 Inch Internal SSD, up to 560MB/s - CT1000MX500SSD1

For some reason I never upgraded the wifi card on my PC even though I got a new router last year, so upgrading to this gave me a notable boost in performance as well as getting better signal strength.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Revolution Cordless Laser Mouse - Laser - USB I bought this mouse for my husband as a Christmas gift. For the most part, he and I are not into technical gadgets, but I thought that a cordless mouse would be more convenient for our home computer setup, and after doing a lot of online research, I decided to go with the Logitech MX. This product looks/feels unlike any mouse I've ever used before. Although it may seem a bit unwieldy at first, however, it actually fits very comfortably into the hand and feels very natural. As other reviewers have mentioned, the mouse glides smoothly over any surface, no mouse pad needed, and the scrolling ability is amazing--there are actually two scrolling modes, one with zero resistance, the other the more traditional click-type scrolling for those who prefer moving more slowly. The mouse has some great features, too, some of which I have yet to fully explore. My favorite is the little search button that lets you highlight text to be searched and then access your favorite search engine automatically. I also like the thumb buttons which allow you to switch back and forth amongst windows and applications, although I have found these to be a bit less intuitive, thereby taking a little longer to get the hang of. Finally, I've been impressed by the battery life--we've had the mouse set up for weeks now and haven't had to change it yet (granted, we average only 2-3 hours computer time per day at home).

The only thing that stopped me from giving this mouse five stars was that we experienced problems during setup. Although everything seemed fine at first and the mouse began working immediately, the SetPoint software that came with the mouse wrecked havoc with our computer, causing a major crash. Someone more computer-savvy might have been able to resolve this issue immediately, but DH and I lost two days to trying to figure out how to correct the problem. Eventually, however, we were able to start the computer in safe mode, delete the SetPoint software, and reload the newest version of the software from the Logitech web site, and we have experienced no further problems since that time. So, as long as you are willing to accept the possibility of some initial installation difficulties, I highly recommend this cool little mouse.

At the time of this review, this Netvue Orb Cam is the same list price as the Netvue Home Cam I previously purchased. Taking into consideration that Netvue Home Cam doesn't have the Pan & Tilt feature that this Cam does, getting added features for the same price is always nice.

Linking this camera to my account was straightforward and easy to do. Also, setup was easier to do than most wifi plugs and wall switches.

My son added my Netvue cameras to my Alexa account and setup Routines so the motion detection turns on lights connected to smart plugs as I walk through the house.

Performance of this Camera matches the quality of my other Netvue Cams and my Ring Doorbell 2 cam.

Pan & Tilt feature is sluggish and does not allow for small adjustment. For me that's not a problem because I won't be changing its angle or position regularly.

As seen in the attached photo, my son installed it at the edge of a window so that the anchor screws went into a stud and the camera wire could be hidden behind a curtain. He moved the surge protector that my cell phone charger and clock plugs into and mounted it on the wall so the camera could be plugged in as it was not long enough to reach the electrical outlet. We had to move furniture around to hide the surge protector.

NOTES:
TO PET OWNERS, if this camera not mounted and is set on a bookcase, the Pan & Tilt feature will not angle down below the level of the item it is sitting on, which means you may not see your pet walking around. I have a German Shepard as a service dog (mobility dog) and I mounted my camera on the wall so I could always see him.

Standard house door is roughly 80" (6' 8") and most home ceiling heights are 8 ft (96") but sometimes 10ft or 12ft. The power cords on all 3 Netvue cameras I own are 6ft (same as a standard household item such as a fan or clock). Every camera has required an extension cord and moving furniture.

I have have read numerous reviews about Smart Home devices complaining they are only 2.4g. 5.0g Wifi has faster transfer speeds but lower reception distances. 2.4g, like this device has, is more reliable with less connection interruptions.

1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver
