text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) UPDATE: After over a year of using these, I have to say that the bad outweighs the good, especially for how expensive they are.

It is true. There is nothing easier to set up. But it's next to useless when you actually need it. They trigger way too slowly. And the batteries are not set up to charge or even work very well when it's really cold out, so even though they are close enough to an outlet for me to charge them without taking them down, I have to bring them inside to charge them when it is cold. But it's the slow trigger that really makes this system not worth the expense.

For example: New Year's Eve, someone wrote Happy New Year in the snow on my windshield. One of my Arlo cameras is pointed right at my car. I have a clip from before it happened. I have a clip from after it happened. If I did not also have wired cameras that record continuously, I would not know whom to thank (our sweet next door neighbors - they are so lovely!).

The cameras make decent deterrents. And they are handy to have when I need a live view of something. But if you want to catch somebody doing something, there are better options.

_____________
Original Review Follows
_____________

I'm going to give you the bad, then the just okay, and then the good. Short version of all that is that I wish these triggered a bit faster and weren't so expensive, but they are a substantial improvement over my older Arlo system. Skip to the end if you want to know how to set up the siren.

Bottom line: This system is not quite perfect, and it is quite expensive, but it is wireless, weatherproof, super easy to set up, and backwards compatible. I would recommend this to a family member or anyone else who needs a wireless outdoor install.

Okay, so the bad (and it isn't really that bad) is that the Arlo Pro cameras have some trigger lag. Depending on how fast the trigger is moving, you may catch them just as they leave the frame, or you might miss them altogether. If it's a person walking, no problem. A person walking briskly? Might be a little problem. Basically, these are better for a zombie apocalypse than for a werewolf invasion. I have a hardwired CCTV DVR system that is always "recording," so when it gets a motion alert, it "starts" the clip five seconds in the past.

The just okay part is that, for this kind of money, I wish the cameras had more configurability. I would like to be able to set the exact parameters of the field I want to monitor (currently, you can pan and zoom but that's not really what I am looking to do), and I would like to be able to set the sensitivity in a meaningful way (I live in a city on a fairly busy street and get hundreds of alerts/clips no matter how I try to minimize them). Additionally, the over-sensitivity is a drain on battery life, which is an indirect functional limitation on where I install the cameras. With batteries needing to be changed/charged within a matter of days, I need to be able to get to these easily.

Now for the good stuff:

I like Arlo a lot. I have three of the old ones, and even with the lag, they are great for outdoor applications. The Arlo Pro cameras are better. The video quality is better. While there is lag, it is not as bad as it is on the older models. These are also BY FAR the easiest cameras to set up and keep running. I have wifi range extenders throughout my weird old condo, and my Arlo cameras never drop their signals.

The Arlo Pro base station will work with your old Arlo cameras. I kept my old base station running, though, so that I can run different cameras on different schedules. It also works with IFTTT and with the Smart Things App.

The Siren was not intuitive to set up, but it is a cool feature. The default is OFF for all cameras, so don't worry about setting it off while you are setting your system up. You activate it in the settings of each camera - camera by camera. You can also trigger it from the smart phone app, so in the event that someone breaks in while you are home, you can turn on the alarm (better for a werewolf invasion than for the zombie apocalypse).

From the Arlo website:
To create a rule that includes a siren trigger:
Launch the Arlo app or log in to your Arlo account at arlo.netgear.com.
Tap or click Mode to access the mode tab.
Tap or click the Arlo Pro base station for which you would like to add a siren trigger.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to the mode that you would like to edit.
Under Rules, tap the pencil icon or click Edit next to the device that you want to trigger the siren.
Select the Turn Siren ON check box.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to Turn Siren ON.
Set the sliders for Siren Duration and Siren Loudness.
Tap < Edit Rule or click Back.
Tap Done or click Save.
Note: This rule is not active until you activate the mode to which you added the siren trigger.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130)

Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming I'm not a gamer. I wanted to try this mouse pad out for graphics (photo editing, vector graphics, and so forth). I'm not a big fan of pen-type tablet input devices. I've always preferred working with a mouse. (To me, the only real down side to using a mouse instead of a tablet input is loss of pressure sensitivity, but there are plenty of workarounds.)

This pad works great. An optical/laser mouse reads it very well, with the slightest movements picked up. The bottom of the pad is grippy enough for the pad to stay put, and the surface, while satin-like, still has enough resistance to provide a lot of fine control.

It's also larger than I expected. It's 11 inches by 13.5 inches. And it is quite flexible and rolls up easily for storage or transport.

Here are some tips for getting precise mouse control:

First of all understand that a low-DPI setting means your pointer doesn't move far when you move the mouse. This enables gamers to aim and target precisely in-game. It also enables artists to precisely move the pointers when working on graphics. How far your cursor/pointer moves is entirely up to you and can be adjusted in your control panel for pointer settings (or, depending on the game, possibly can be adjusted in your game settings).

In that control panel, uncheck "enhance pointer precision." This will turn off pointer acceleration, which can adversely affect control. If the software (or game) you're using overrides this (rare in graphics software, but more common in games), you may have to employ a fix. Just do a search for "Windows 7/8 mouse fix" and you'll find plenty of information on how to do this.

Anyway, it's a great pad for precision cursor control with a mouse, whether for gaming or graphics.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming

Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000 Though I have a laptop, I decided to use this solid-state drive as a boot drive on my desktop computer. If you are unfamiliar with the difference between a solid-state and a regular hard drive, the solid-state has no moving parts, which makes it silent, fast, reliable, and shock resistant. It has twice the capacity and twice the speed of the solid-state drive I got a couple of years ago for the same price, and blows away a standard drive for speed.

Given the silence and speed, it makes a great boot drive for running Windows, Photoshop, and other programs where speed is a huge advantage. Just to give you an idea, when upgrading from a regular two-year-old hard drive to this solid-state drive, my Windows boot time went from two minutes to about 10 seconds. Seriously, my computer now starts up and is ready to use in like 10 seconds.

What I do is use a solid-state drive as my boot drive and a regular hard drive as a storage drive. Solid-state drives like this are really expensive to purchase if you need any kind of capacity, but a 200 GB drive will certainly hold all of your programs and often used files.

As for this drive specifically, I hooked it up to my desktop and it was immediately recognized by Windows. The drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up as a drive and work in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

As I said, it's a lot faster than the solid-state drive I had from a couple years ago, and there's no problem using it on my desktop machine rather than my laptop.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000

Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black Before you buy, check the Monoprice website for this item. The price may be much cheaper over there.

This is a very inexpensive, relatively low quality TV antenna. You get what you pay for. They advertise this for both indoor and outdoor use, but the mostly plastic construction will not last long outdoors in areas that get a lot of wind, ice, or bright sunlight. The attached 3 foot cable really tells you what their intended use case is. If your TV is near a window, hang the antenna in the window, plug it in, and you're done.

The advertised 50 mile range is for ideal conditions, mounting the antenna outdoors in an area where there are absolutely no obstructions between your home and the TV broadcast tower (no trees, no buildings, etc). Expect much worse range for an indoor mounting and if there are any obstructions. If you live in an area with trees etc, you should get a more sturdy antenna that can be mounted on a pole on top of your roof so it can receive a signal over the trees.

This antenna is advertised for UHF frequencies only. Most TV stations use UHF these days, but in my area there are a couple that use VHF and this antenna is not usable for those channels. If you really want VHF, I suggest getting a different antenna from this one.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black

Overall, a nice headphone but you can get something very similar at a fraction of the price.

I had high hopes for the OontZ Angle since I have been using an OontZ Curve also made by Cambridge Sound Works for over 2 years without a single problem. In my humble opinion the OontZ Curve sounds a little better than OontZ Angle but not being splash proof it does not meet my needs at this time. text_fidelity_a:
Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops I've used much worse keyboards and mice, but I've also used much better. The keyboard is not bad, but speed typists would definitely prefer better. Because this is a full-size keyboard, be aware that you'll need ample space on your pull-out keyboard drawer. Some office desks have very narrow and shallow drawers. The mouse is okay too but feels a little cheap. However, this product was obviously not intended to be top-end.

My main criticism of this package is the somewhat confusing owner's manual. Every USB product I've used, particularly a kb or mouse, are plug-and-play. The manual gave instructions for "repairing' with the device, and it was unclear why you would need to issue the series of key commands in order to reconnect via USB on a PC. Perhaps this connection procedure applies only to other types of devices. After one brief failed attempt to connect (see next paragraph), the second try connected okay after I plugged in the USB dongle. I also unplugged/replugged the dongle and it worked again, without having to issue any of the "Esc + K" keypresses that the manual stated were necessary to repair the devices.

I suspect the range of this pairing is not very far. The first time I plugged the dongle in, neither the kb nor the mouse worked. I had to move both closer to the dongle before I got them to connect. The kb and mouse were only four feet from the dongle when I first installed them. After I finally got everything to connect at close range, I moved the kb and mouse back to the distance of four feet, and they continued to work. So I'm not sure of what distance would cause a disconnect.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops
